A retry with the same `idempotency_key` must use the same arguments, with `pgledger_create_transfers` requests in the same order (see Batch Ordering), or an error will be returned:

PostgreSQL has several transaction isolation levels. Under Read Committed (the default), concurrent calls with the same `idempotency_key` will wait for each other, and the later ones will return the transfers created from the first call if the requests match. Under Repeatable Read or Serializable, the later calls cannot see transfers created after the start of their own transaction snapshot. So instead of returning the existing transfers, the call will fail and should be re-tried in a new transaction.

Phrag implements its approach to creating GraphQL from an RDBMS connection for instant, flexible and customizable CRUD operations.

- **Instantly Operational:** Phrag creates a GraphQL simply from a RDBMS connection, retrieving schema data of tables, columns, primary keys and foreign keys. It can run as part of a Clojure project or stand-alone releases.

- **CRUD Features:** tables and/or views become queryable as root objects including nested objects of n-ary relationships with aggregation, filter, sorting and pagination supported. Mutations (`create`, `update` and `delete`) are also created per table.

- **Customization:** Phrag comes with an interceptor capability to customize behaviors of GraphQL. Custom functions can be configured per table & operation type and at pre/post DB operations. It can make a GraphQL service more practical with access controls, event firing and more.

- **Performance in Mind:** Phrag's query resolver translates a nested object query into a single SQL query, leveraging correlated subqueries and JSON functions. Load tests have also been performed to verify it scales linear with resources without obvious bottlenecks.
- **Practicality in Mind:** Phrag was developed side by side with a POC project to verify its concept and validate the practicality.

问数系统要落地,安全边界不能是提示词里的一句请求。下面这些**全是代码,不是模型行为**(完整清单见安全边界):
|**只读防火墙**|SQL 过 AST 解析后判定:非查询语句、任何 DML/DDL、`SELECT INTO OUTFILE`、危险函数、元数据表一律拒绝,不靠关键字黑名单|
|**表级 allowlist**|闸设在**执行路径本身**(`execute` / `explain` 都过),所以从 MCP、语义查询 API 或任何旁路进来的 SQL 同样受限|
|**执行代价护栏**|执行前用 EXPLAIN 估算最重算子行数,超软限(默认 5000 万)打回生成节点补 `LIMIT`,超硬限直接拒绝,不烧一轮 LLM 重生成|
|**字段级脱敏**|按字段声明 `partial` / `hash` / `null`,在结果出库、任何面向模型的节点之前改写;失败方向取严——该脱敏而读不出 salt 或语义模型,拒绝这次查询,不降级放行|

|**行/列级授权**|主体 grant **只收窄、不授予**:行谓词以表引用子查询重写(顶层 WHERE 在子查询/UNION 里会把内层别名提到外层),被禁列在任何位置被引用即拒——`SELECT *` 拒绝、`COUNT(*)` 放行;解析不出别名或列就拒绝执行。主链、`/v1/semantic/query`、生成期 probe/check/search、候选投票与归因共用同一个 scope 引擎;管理员豁免,定时任务按任务所有者身份运行|
|**模型出境治理**|工具回喂给模型的探测行与查值结果,在进上下文前按语义层 `mask` 声明脱敏——以 `principal=None` 运行,管理员也不能把声明字段原文发给模型;脱敏失败整条观测作废,绝不回落原文。provider 白名单在网关调用前判定,拒绝不触网;审计只记字段名,不记值|
|**不可信内容隔离**|数据库单元格内容(以及检索、探测结果)先过注入扫描,命中即替换为隔离占位符再进提示;人确认过的 KB 内容不在此列|
|**限流、配额与审计**|按用户令牌桶与每日配额,超限 429;每次执行记录 question / SQL / verdict / 行数 / 耗时 / 错误|
|**行动只提案,不执行**|判定触发只把行动冻结成提案(载荷创建即定稿、幂等键去重),批准后才外送;行动层**不接数据源连接器**——系统自身没有写回业务库的通道,批准、外送与回执各自独立留痕|
|认证组件缺失|拒绝启动|宁可起不来,也不静默地不安全|
|人在环的载荷认不出|默认拒绝|不执行,交给人|
|脱敏读不出 salt 或语义模型|拒绝执行|不降级为明文交付|
|行/列 scope 解析不出表或列|拒绝执行|不猜别名,也不放宽成不过滤|
|工具回喂脱敏失败|整条观测作废|绝不把原文交给模型|
|OIDC state / 签名 / 受众校验不通过|拒绝登录|不签发令牌;失败码经前端 fragment 提示|
|拿不到授权依据(`None`)|拒绝一切|「忘了授权」不退化成放行|
|只读自检查不成|记「未验证」|绝不渲染成「安全」|
|KB 漂移检查读不出来,或 L3 有声明判不了|非零退出码(部分判不了 → 2)|不把「没查成」当「没问题」|
|置信度判定不出|倒向最保守的档|虚低好过虚高|
|噪声带测不出(块数不足 / 无历史)|如实记「判不了」|要求噪声带兜底的规则宁可报错误运行,不静默放行|
同样的取向也写在别处:健康检查区分 `unavailable` 与 `degraded`(而不是一个「挂了」),规则链第一条失败即止(而不是给一堆模糊提示),掩码失败清空结果集(而不是留一份可能泄漏的旧结果)。完整清单见安全边界与可观测性。

The single-module codebase groups `auth`, `book`, `loan`, `user`, `audit`, and `info` by feature, then by layer. Controllers accept and return DTOs; services own business rules, transactions, and entity-to-DTO mapping; repositories own persistence. |Introduced shared not-found and invalid-request exception types|Expected client errors have consistent status codes; unexpected faults get a generic 500 response.|
|Layered the test profile over runtime configuration|Tests exercise the real application defaults with only test-specific overrides.|
|Entity types and database columns disagreed at startup|Made Flyway the sole schema authority, aligned migrations with JPA, and kept Hibernate schema validation enabled.|
|Container startup could race PostgreSQL readiness|Added a database health check and made the app wait for a healthy database.|
|Concurrent checkout could assign one copy twice|Added row locking, a database unique index for active loans, and PostgreSQL concurrency tests.|
|HTTP-only or mocked tests could miss real persistence errors|Split fast unit/MVC tests from Testcontainers integration tests that exercise migrations, JPA, constraints, and loan races.|
|Scattered account rules and error handling were hard to audit|Centralized target-role/ownership checks in `UserAccessPolicy` and mapped client failures through shared exception types.|

Constraints declared in a model's yaml are applied when — and only when — the model's contract is enforced, which is what every dbt adapter does and keeps their cost opt-in. (dbt-core does not raise if you declare constraints with the contract off — they are simply never emitted.) `not_null`, `check`, `unique`, `primary_key` and `foreign_key` are all supported.
The full set of rules, with the test that verifies each, is in docs/constraints.md.

`primary_key` and `unique` are emitted as `NONCLUSTERED` by default so they can coexist with the clustered columnstore index built for `as_columnstore`. Use dbt's own `expression` field to ask for something else:
The adapter ships a macro for exactly this, meant as a `pre_hook` on the **referenced** (parent) model:

It drops the foreign keys in both directions — the inbound ones other tables hold against this model, and this model's own outbound ones — so the rebuild's backup drop succeeds. The trade-off is explicit and worth stating: **the child's foreign key does not exist between the parent's rebuild and the child's next build.** (dbt-postgres makes the same trade silently, by issuing every `drop table` with `cascade`.)

Add the hook *before* the first rebuild. Once a rebuild has failed with `Msg 3726`, the new table is already in place but without its own named constraints — those are applied after the backup drop that failed — and the child's key now points at `<model>__dbt_backup`, because a foreign key follows the object, not the name. A plain `dbt run` does not recover: the parent trips over the same backup and the child is skipped behind it. Rebuild the child alone — that run fails too, since the parent has no key to reference, but its swap drops the old child and the stale key with it — and a plain `dbt run` then rebuilds both in order. Dropping the child's key by hand (`ALTER TABLE <child> DROP CONSTRAINT <name>`) does the same.

`table_refresh_method: dml` is *not* a workaround. Its steady-state refresh issues `DELETE FROM <parent>`, which fails with `Msg 547` as soon as the child holds referencing rows, and its schema-change path falls back to the same rename-swap, hitting `Msg 3726` anyway.

An *unnamed* `primary_key` or `unique` constraint on a column that also carries a data mask is rejected by the build. The constraint rides the `CREATE TABLE`, so its index already exists by the time `apply_masks` runs, and the adapter refuses to mask any column that an index has as a key: *is configured for masking but is also an index key column*. Declare that constraint at the model level **with a `name:`** instead — named constraints are applied by `ALTER TABLE` after the masks are in place, which the adapter allows.

The adapter can apply SQL Server Dynamic Data Masking (DDM) to columns as part of the materialization, so masks are re-applied on every build and survive dbt's drop-and-recreate on a full refresh. A principal granted `SELECT` but not `UNMASK` then sees masked values instead of real data (dbt's own build principal, being `db_owner`, keeps `UNMASK` and reads real data). Requires **SQL Server 2016+**.
